Rachel — thanks for the note. Attaching the requested diagram and an egress excerpt; included a short narrative below that you can drop into the SOC 2 packet. Happy to hop on a 30-minute screen share if the auditor wants to walk it live.

High-level summary (for packet):
- Key ownership: Customer keys are supported via customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for Private deployments; for Redwood-hosted Dedicated we offer tenant-specific keys stored in our KMS with optional HSM-backed key wrapping.
- KMS flow: Customer data is encrypted at rest with per-tenant data keys. Per-token ephemeral encryption keys are derived during model serving; key wrapping/unwrapping happens in the KMS control plane that is logically separated from the inference data path. The attached PNG shows the control-plane call pattern and the minimal metadata exchanged (key IDs, signatures).
- Control plane vs data plane: Control-plane calls (orchestration, key requests) route over a management network that does not carry raw inference payloads. The inference data path between GPU hosts and customer application instances is isolated via VLAN/VRF and mTLS tunnels; control messages reference keys but do not include plaintext PII or model outputs.
- Egress controls: See attached CSV excerpt; outbound flows to external services are restricted to a documented set of IP ranges and FQDNs. For Private/on-prem we provide a hardened egress appliance pattern (edge proxy) that customers can put in front of the runtime.

Deliverables attached: redwood_kms_flow_v1.drawio.png, transit-gateway-acl-excerpt.pdf, egress-ip-whitelist.csv

If helpful, I can add a short mapping table to SIG/CAIQ—Markus and Laura, can you confirm the exact wording for the "control plane does not carry PII" sentence and whether we should call out HSM vendor options?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Rachel / team — quick technical clarifications to drop into the auditor packet. Please quote-permission these items: feel free to paste verbatim.

- KMS hosting options: Private (customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS or on-prem HSM) or Redwood-hosted with HSM-backed key wrapping (FIPS 140-2 L3-certified HSMs supported). Customer can supply root keys via envelope encryption — we never store customer root material unwrapped.
- Key lifetime and rotation: Data keys are per-tenant and rotated on configurable schedules; master key rotation requires re-wrapping but not full data re-encryption in the common case. Rotation proofs and KMS audit logs are available and can be exported for SOC 2 evidence.
- Control/data plane separation: Control plane runs in a dedicated management VPC with enforced ACLs and a separate NAT/eBGP egress. Inference hosts only accept mTLS connections from customer ingress proxies (certificate validation enforced). The PNG shows a dashed line for the management plane; the only tokens crossing are key IDs and short-lived signed grants.
- Transit gateway notes: For Dedicated deployments that use a transit gateway, we push granular route maps and prefix-lists so customer CIDR blocks are isolated. The attached ACL excerpt is an example excerpt we can redact for external distribution.
- Egress filtering: Outbound destinations are an allowlist. For hosted Dedicated we maintain a published IP/FQDN list that auditors can retrieve via a signed link; for Private deployments customers can enforce their own egress proxies.

If you need a one-paragraph attestation for SOC 2 stating "keys are never exported in plaintext from KMS; control plane does not persist inference payloads", I can draft that and Laura can add compliance language.

-Markus Klein
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
